information: HARDLINE RULE: Never use the stock system /usr/bin/sqlite3 CLI to inspect a libSQL database. It lacks libSQL's vector extension, so a bare `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM memory` (or similar) against a table with a vector index gets silently satisfied via an unusable `libsql_vector_idx` path and returns 0 rows instead of erroring — there is no warning that the query didn't actually execute against real data. This produced a false "all data has been lost" incident report during a debugging session, triggering unnecessary panic and recovery work. Correct approaches: use the `@libsql/client` npm/bun package to query, or if you must use a sqlite3-family CLI, force `COUNT(*) ... NOT INDEXED` to bypass the broken vector-index path.

INCIDENT: Test suite deleting the production database. Streams/store-auto-adapter.test.ts in swarm-mail had an afterEach hook calling rm(getDatabasePath(), { force: true }) against the real ~/.config/swarm-tools/swarm.db. Root cause: swarm-mail package had no bunfig.toml preload setting SWARM_DB_PATH, unlike sibling packages (e.g. swarm-queue) that document that pattern; any test run without an explicit override resolved getDatabasePath() to the production path and then deleted it. Fix: added bunfig.toml + test-preload.ts forcing a temp DB path for the package's test run, plus a runtime guard that throws if a test process resolves to the production database path. Prevention: every package with DB-touching tests needs its own bunfig.toml preload — do not assume it's inherited from siblings.

Workspace now 61/61 packages, all typecheck green, spot-checked 3 (wallet, orm, pac-man) all RED at genuine `throw new Error("Not implemented")` — no config/import errors. Multi-file-system-sounding katas (ORM, Social Network, CQRS Booking, JEE WebAuthentication, PacMan) were still scaffolded with the same single-function stub template per instructions — do not over-engineer scaffolds for katas that "sound" like they need multiple files.

Moon 2.4.6 gotchas for bun/TS monorepo root config: (1) bare `moon` on PATH can be a stale proto shim (2.2.5) while `bunx moon` resolves the pinned devDependency version (2.4.6) — always use `bunx moon` and verify both with `moon --version` vs `bunx moon --version` if config uses newer fields. (2) `.moon/toolchains.yml` needs BOTH `bun: { version }` AND `javascript: { packageManager: 'bun' }` — bun alone doesn't register the JS toolchain. (3) Inherited tasks for all projects go in `.moon/tasks/all.yml` (directory form), NOT singular `.moon/tasks.yml` (removed in 2.0). (4) `moon run <target>` has NO `--dry-run` flag in 2.4.6 — that flag doesn't exist; use `moon query projects`/`moon query tasks` (exit 0, JSON output) to validate config parses without executing anything. (5) `moon check --all` requires a TTY or explicit project IDs even with --all in some setups — throws `app::tty::required_id`; not reliable for non-interactive CI-style verification. (6) With zero projects yet (empty packages/*), `moon run :test` correctly emits 'No tasks found. Unable to execute action pipeline' with exit 1 — this is expected/correct behavior, not a config error, since inherited tasks only materialize once a project exists to inherit them.

DECISION: Switching embedding model to nomic-embed-text at 768 dimensions REJECTED. Warm median latency 23.71ms vs current mxbai-embed-large's 23.79ms — a statistical wash, which matters because speed was the entire stated rationale for considering the switch. Quality is also worse: MTEB ~62.3 for nomic vs ~64.7 for mxbai. The migration cost would have been real: an F32_BLOB(1024) -> F32_BLOB(768) schema/vector-index migration, plus a second hand-patch of a 440K-line vendored bundle to inject the `search_document:` / `search_query:` prefixes that nomic requires on every embed call (mxbai needs no such prefixing). Confirmed this isn't just theoretical prefix hygiene: omitting those prefixes measurably CHANGED the #1 ranked result for a test query in a side-by-side comparison — a real ranking regression, not just a score-calibration nuance. Conclusion: no speed win, quality loss, nontrivial migration cost — reject.

PROCEDURE: moon build tool version trap in this environment — always invoke as `bunx moon`, never bare `moon`. A bare `moon` on PATH can resolve to a stale proto-managed shim (observed at version 2.2.5) instead of the project-pinned 2.4.6, silently running the wrong toolchain version with different behavior/flags. Also verified: `moon run --dry-run` does not exist as a flag in moon 2.x (it's a 1.x-only flag, will error), and `moon check --all` has a TTY-detection quirk that misbehaves in non-interactive/shells. For config validation instead of a dry-run, use `moon query` (e.g. `moon query projects`, `moon query tasks`) to inspect resolved config without executing anything.

INCIDENT: Read-only access wiping the libSQL database under concurrency. createLibSQLAdapter forced `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on every connection open, including pure read-only calls — and connection-open-on-every-call is the near-universal entry point for MCP tool calls, each of which is a fresh short-lived process/connection. Concurrent processes racing truncating WAL checkpoints lost pages. Reproduced deliberately at 600 concurrent read-only connections: 382 SQLITE_BUSY errors + 10 SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY errors, matching the error signature seen in production logs. Fix: removed the forced per-open checkpoint entirely (checkpointing moved to a best-effort call on close() instead), set busy_timeout to 10s, added a shared retry-with-backoff wrapper around connection acquisition. Post-fix validation: 0 errors at the same 600-concurrent-connection load. Prevention: never force a TRUNCATE checkpoint on connection open in a libSQL/SQLite adapter that may be opened concurrently by many short-lived processes — checkpoint on close or on an explicit maintenance path only.

Doc-service foundation (katas epic msj0nhchrv2, cell msj0nhcm75v): built packages/doc-service in swarm-tools monorepo. Key design decision — portability is enforced by dependency graph, not repo location: the package has zero deps on swarm-mail/hive/any internal package, only zod. This lets it be pm pack'd into a standalone repo later with no rewrite. Sanitization-by-omission: the IR (DocumentationCorpus) has no field anywhere for /session/identity — Provenance.author is contractually human/org-identity-only. This means the downstream sanitization gate cell doesn't have to scrub rendered markdown; it validates the corpus once before any generator sees it. Generated-vs-authored marker convention: front-matter `generated: true` (exact boolean match, no truthy coercion) is the ONLY signal; absence = human-owned by default, which fails safe (a generator bug that omits the marker fails toward "orphaned but preserved" not "silently overwritten").

DECISION: Forked joelhooks/swarm-tools on GitHub rather than waiting for the upstream fix to land, for the status-quoting bug (see the "silent total search failure" incident memory). Upstream `main` had received no fix commit since 2026-02-23, and the npm package had been unpublished since 2026-02-06 — so even a merged fix would not have been installable via normal `bun add`. Decisive evidence for forking rather than waiting: PR #186, which contained the exact fix for the status-default bug, was auto-closed same-day by an unvouched-contributor bot policy on the upstream repo — meaning the correct fix already existed publicly but was structurally blocked from ever landing on main. Conclusion: forking was the only path to an installable fix; there was no reasonable "just wait" option.

INCIDENT: Test pollution at scale from missing DB isolation. Opencode-swarm-plugin's 2,127-test suite had the same missing test-isolation problem as swarm-mail (no bunfig.toml preload override) and wrote 4,646 rows plus 100+ scratch project keys directly into the production database over the course of normal test runs. Of the resulting corpus, only 14 rows were real/legitimate data — the rest was test pollution. This is the same root cause class as the swarm-mail incident (missing SWARM_DB_PATH override) but at 2,127x the blast radius due to suite size. Prevention: audit every package in the monorepo for a DB-path-overriding bunfig.toml before trusting `bun test` output against a shared/production database path.

HARDLINE RULE: A `healthy: true` status field is not a valid health signal on its own — verify with a real round-trip instead. During this session, the hive/swarm-tools health check reported `healthy: true` under two conditions where the system was actually broken: (1) with 0 rows and 0 embeddings in the corpus (effectively an empty, useless index), and (2) with 4,646 polluted test rows mixed into production data (a corrupted, untrustworthy index). In both cases the boolean health flag gave no indication anything was wrong. Correct verification method: perform an actual store() followed by a find() for that same content and confirm it comes back with a sensible similarity score — a functional round-trip test, not a status field that can be true independent of whether search actually works.

PROCEDURE: moon 2.x template and config schema differs meaningfully from 1.x, verified by hand while debugging config errors. Templates live at `<workspaceRoot>/templates/`, NOT `.moon/templates/` (the 1.x location — using it silently means moon never finds your templates, no error). The scaffolding field is `toolchains` (plural, array) in 2.x, replacing the 1.x singular `toolchain`/`platform` fields. The 1.x `local: true` task option does not exist in v2 at all — the v2 equivalent is either `preset: 'utility'` or explicit `options: { cache: false, runInCI: false }`. Tera template filename interpolation syntax also changed: use SQUARE brackets for variable interpolation in generated filenames, e.g. `src/[name | kebab_case].ts`, not the old curly-brace style.

HARDLINE RULE: Never run `bun test` from a monorepo root directory when the suite touches a DB-backed package. Running from root skips the package-local bunfig.toml preload that sets SWARM_DB_PATH (or equivalent test-DB-override env var) — that preload only activates when bun test's working directory matches the package containing the bunfig.toml. The practical effect is that tests silently hit the real production database instead of an isolated test DB, with no warning that isolation was skipped. Always `cd` into the specific package directory before running `bun test` on packages with DB-touching suites; do not rely on root-level `bun test` recursing safely into subpackages for these cases.

RETROSPECTIVE ROOT CAUSE: swarm_complete was broken for the entire session that produced these findings, and its fallback/error path silently skipped outcome recording (no learning got stored, no error surfaced to the operator). This is why 18 verified findings — incidents, decisions, and hardline rules discovered through real debugging and benchmarking — existed only in session transcripts and were never recorded into hive's long-term memory corpus, leaving the documentation service that reads this corpus far thinner than the actual work performed. Prevention: any completion/recording path that can silently no-op on failure needs either a hard failure (throw, don't swallow) or an explicit "recording skipped" signal surfaced to the operator, so gaps like this are caught immediately rather than discovered later via manual backfill.

PROCEDURE: Verified global install/upgrade flow for opencode-swarm-plugin: `bun pm pack` -> `bun remove -g opencode-swarm-plugin` -> `bun add -g <tarball-path>`. Critical gotcha: `bun pm pack` does NOT bundle `workspace:*` dependencies into the resulting tarball — each workspace dependency (e.g. swarm-mail) must be packed and globally installed as its own separate step, or the global install will reference a workspace protocol that doesn't resolve outside the monorepo. Verified rollback path if a bad version gets installed globally: `bun remove -g opencode-swarm-plugin swarm-mail && bun add -g opencode-swarm-plugin@0.63.2` (pin to last known-good version explicitly).

MOON 2.x TEMPLATES - LOCATION & REGISTRATION (verified moonrepo.dev v2 docs, installed @moonrepo/cli 2.4.6, katas repo). Default template search path is `<workspaceRoot>/templates/` NOT `.moon/templates/` (original assumption was wrong - flag as corrected)..moon/workspace.yml `generator.templates` defaults to `./templates`; since our workspace.yml has no `generator:` block, moon auto-discovers `./templates/<name>/template.yml` with NO registration needed. To use a custom location (e.g..moon/templates/) you must set:
generator:
templates:
- './templates'
- './.moon/templates'
Also supports glob://, git://, npm:// locators for sharing templates across repos.

DECISION: MLX/oMLX embedding migration REJECTED for hive/swarm-tools, evaluated twice with fresh benchmarks each time. Warm single-call medians (n=20, discard-first run, identical input string): Ollama+mxbai-embed-large 23.79ms, oMLX+mxbai-embed-large 38.64ms, oMLX+bge-small 15.46ms. oMLX is 1.62x SLOWER than Ollama on the single-call embedding pattern that hivemind_store/hivemind_find actually use in production — oMLX's commonly-cited ~3x batch-throughput advantage is theoretical here because these code paths embed exactly one string per call, never a batch. RAM footprint also worse under MLX: 1.26GB resident at fp32 vs 686MB for the current Ollama F16 model. Additionally, nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (a candidate replacement model) has NO MLX build at all — verified directly against the HuggingFace API — only mxbai-embed-large-v1 (1024-dim) and the small tier bge-small-en-v1.5 / all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (both 384-dim) exist as MLX conversions across a 31-model org inventory that was fully enumerated. Conclusion: do not revisit MLX for this workload unless the access pattern changes to true batched embedding.

PROCEDURE: Required build order in the swarm-tools monorepo is swarm-queue -> swarm-mail -> opencode-swarm-plugin. This order is mandatory (not just conventional) because each package's package.json `main` field points into its own `dist/` directory, and downstream packages import from those `main` entrypoints at build/typecheck time — so a dependency's dist/ must already exist before a dependent package's build will succeed. Building out of order produces missing-module errors that look like a real bug but are just a build-order violation.

HARDLINE RULE: A fix is not live just because it is committed and even rebuilt — verify the actually-running artifact. During this session, a long-running MCP host process had cached previously-loaded code in memory and kept serving pre-fix behavior even after the source was fixed and rebuilt, because the host was never restarted to pick up the new dist/ output. This caused the stale code to continue polluting the database during the very task whose purpose was to fix that pollution — actively working against the fix while appearing to have already applied it. Prevention: after any fix to a long-running service/MCP host, explicitly verify the installed/running artifact (e.g. Grep the loaded file on disk for the fix, or check a version/build marker) rather than trusting that a rebuild + commit implies the running process picked it up. When verifying data-layer state specifically, prefer direct DB queries over going through the (possibly stale) tool/service layer.

Working generator invocation: `bunx moon generate kata --to packages/<name> -- --name "x" --title "X" --description "..." --source "url"` (note the `--` separator before vars). INCIDENT: Non-idempotent sync duplicating the memory corpus after recovery. importSingleMemory() deduped incoming records only by exact `id`, and was content-blind (no check on the actual memory text/embedding). hivemind_store mints a fresh random id on every call, so when memories were rehydrated/restored after a wipe, they were assigned new ids different from their originals. The next JSONL sync then read the git-tracked JSONL (which still held the pre-wipe original ids), matched none of them against the new-id rows now in the DB, and re-inserted all 14 as duplicates — bringing the DB to 28 rows — then a subsequent export step wrote all 28 back out, poisoning the git-tracked JSONL file itself with duplicates. Fix: importSingleMemory() now does a content-equality check (not just id equality) before inserting. Prevention: any restore/rehydrate path that can produce new ids for logically-same records needs content-based dedup, not id-based, or it will duplicate on every subsequent sync cycle.

MOON 2.x template.yml SCHEMA (verified). Example:
id: 'kata'
title: 'Coding Kata'
description: |
Scaffolds a new coding kata package with test file, source stub, moon tasks.
Destination: 'packages/[name | kebab_case]'
extends: ['base']
variables:
name:
type: 'string'
required: true
prompt: 'Kata name (kebab-case, e.g. Four-squares)?'
default: ''
`type` accepts: array, boolean, string, object, number, enum (no float support - use string). Enum supports `values` (list of string or {value,label}), `multiple: true`, `default`. `required` enforced only during prompting. `internal: true` (v1.23+) prevents CLI-arg overrides of that var. `order` (v1.23+) controls prompt sequence. `destination` supports `[varName]` bracket interpolation with filters, relative to CWD unless prefixed with `/` (workspace root relative).

HARDLINE RULE: Always back up before any schema migration or bulk delete, and always to a NEW timestamped filename (never overwrite the previous backup). During this session there were four separate data-loss incidents in a single day (status-quoting bug, test-suite DB deletion, WAL-checkpoint concurrency wipe, and sync duplication) — manual timestamped backups taken before risky operations were the only reason all four were fully recoverable. Explicitly noted as a process gap: this discipline was manual and should not remain load-bearing — backup rotation before migrations/bulk-deletes should be automated so recovery doesn't depend on someone remembering to `cp` the DB file first.

MOON 2.x moon.yml for bun/TS kata. Field name is toolchains (plural array) not toolchain/platform (v1 name, deprecated). Local:true task field NOT FOUND in v2 docs - v1-only, use preset:'utility' or options:{cache:false,runInCI:false} instead. Recommended moon.yml: language:'typescript', layer:'library', tasks omitted (inherited). Language values: bash,batch,go,javascript,php,python,ruby,rust,typescript,unknown,custom. Layer values: application,automation,configuration,library,scaffolding,tool,unknown - kata fits library. Stack optional, omit for katas. If overriding tasks: command='bun test'/'tsc --noEmit', inputs=['*.ts','*.test.ts'], omit outputs (no build artifacts). Args field appends to inherited command; command is full invocation.

INCIDENT: Silent total search failure in hive/swarm-tools memory store. hivemind_find returned 0 results for every query while hivemind_stats reported a healthy corpus with valid embeddings — indistinguishable from an empty index, no error surfaced. Root cause: Drizzle schema db/schema/memory.ts had `status: text("status").default("'active'")` — literal quote characters baked into the string default. Drizzle's SQLite dialect binds `.default()` as a client-side insert parameter when a column is omitted from `.values()`, regardless of the raw DDL default (which was correct — that's why it survives casual inspection of the schema/migration). store() never explicitly set `status`, so every row got the 7-character literal `'active'` (with quotes) instead of `active`. search()/ftsSearch() filter `WHERE status = 'active'`, which never matched since stored value was `'active'` with quote chars. Proven experimentally: filtering matched 0/13 rows; widening the filter matched 13/13. Cosine similarity scores were always fine (0.33–0.67 against a 0.3 threshold) — rows never survived the WHERE clause, so the vector search itself was never the problem. Fix: set status explicitly in store(), and/or fix the Drizzle default to not include literal quotes. Prevention: when a Drizzle column has a string.default(), verify the client-bound value matches the raw DDL default — they can silently diverge.

DECISION: Vendored (copy-pasted) term/logic code into the fork instead of depending on it via a subdirectory git dependency, despite that re-duplicating logic that had been deliberately deduplicated into a shared location. Verified empirically with real `bun install` runs that Bun does NOT support subdirectory git dependencies of the form `github:owner/repo#main&path:subdir` — the install 404s because bun fetches a tarball for a git ref that is literally treated as containing the string "&path:" rather than parsing it as a subdirectory selector. This was cross-checked against bun's own documentation, which confirms no subdirectory support for git-protocol deps. Npm publish of the shared package was also blocked (no publish auth available, and publishing would make private/internal code public, which was not acceptable). Tradeoff explicitly accepted: code duplication is the cost of avoiding both a broken dependency mechanism and an unwanted public npm publish.
